check: Quotes checked by script: 11 of 11 found on the cited slide.

main.title: The deck recommends the booking app but never says what it costs or who sets it up.
main.why: The board is asked to approve a change it cannot price, and nobody is named to start it.

findings.title: The recommendation has no cost, owner or first step
findings.next: Add who sets the app up, what it costs per year and the first step for next month.

quotes.text: We recommend adopting a volunteer booking app.
Next steps: explore options with the board

findings.why: The board approves budget lines. Without a yearly cost and a named owner it cannot say yes, so the decision slides to the next meeting.
findings.ask: Did the client give the team a budget ceiling?

findings.title: The summary promises a pilot that slide 15 never gives
findings.next: Make slide 15 deliver the pilot the summary describes, or bring the summary down to what the deck supports.

quotes.text: A three-month pilot will test the app with two shift teams.
Next steps: explore options with the board

findings.why: A board member who reads only the summary expects a pilot ready to run. The closing slide asks them to keep exploring instead.
findings.ask: Is the pilot agreed with the client, or the team's own idea?

findings.title: Nobody can tell if 30% unfilled shifts is bad
findings.next: Name what the 30% should be compared with: last year, a similar food bank, or the client's own target.

quotes.text: 30% of shifts are unfilled at least once a month

findings.why: The case for change rests on this number. Without last year's figure or a target, the board cannot tell a crisis from normal churn.
findings.ask: Does the client track a target fill rate?

findings.title: The adoption claim rests on 12 volunteers reached on WhatsApp
findings.next: Optional: say who the survey did not reach, next to the claim on slide 9.

quotes.text: Most volunteers would use an app (9 of 12 surveyed)
Survey sent to the volunteer WhatsApp group

findings.why: Volunteers already on WhatsApp are the ones most likely to use an app. The ones the change could lose were not asked.
findings.ask: How many volunteers are in the WhatsApp group?

findings.title: Analysis titles name topics, not conclusions
findings.next: Optional: rewrite each analysis title as the finding it proves.
findings.why: A board member flipping through slides 7 to 12 learns the topics but not what the team found, so the argument only lives in the speaker's head.
findings.ask: Will the team present this, or will it be read without them?

works.title: The interview synthesis is concrete
works.quote: Coordinators spend about 4 hours a week chasing replies

works.title: The options are compared side by side
works.quote: Option comparison: WhatsApp, shared spreadsheet, booking app
